messages:
maria: FYI — customer reported reranking endpoint returning either a 400 ("input must be an array") or weird identical scores (all 1.0). They attached the cURL from our console snippet and it looks like the example in docs has inconsistent Content-Type / data flags.

maria: Customer's exact curl (copy-pasted from console):
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.inference/v1/rerank \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data' \\n  --data-binary '{"query":"best travel laptops","documents":"[\"Dell XPS 13\", \"MacBook Air\"]"}'
```

maria: They said server returned 200 but scores were `[1.0, 1.0]`. When they switched to `Content-Type: application/json` and `--data-raw` it returned a 400 saying `input must be an array`. So two failure modes.

ken: Repro attempt, trying to parse their payload locally. My suspicion: the docs/console snippets accidentally serialize `documents` as a JSON string instead of an array (notice `"documents":"[...]"`). That would make the server treat the whole thing as a string payload and fall back or coerce. Also `multipart/form-data` vs `application/json` mismatch can cause the client to send form-encoded body.

ken: Quick repro I ran (works as expected):
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.inference/v1/rerank \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  --data-raw '{"query":"best travel laptops","documents":["Dell XPS 13","MacBook Air"]}'
```

ken: That returns 200 with scores like `[0.73, 0.12]` (expected). If you send `"documents":"[...]"` you'll either hit a validation error or the model will attempt to rerank the string as a single document, hence identical scores.

ryan: Ugh, I see the problem. Our docs page has two examples: the console snippet (auto-generated) uses multipart for upload forms and the quick cURL uses `--data-binary` with single quotes. Some shells will strip/interpret quotes differently which can further mangle the JSON.

ryan: Also saw a copy of the console UI cURL where we escape the array with backslashes which ends up as a literal string on paste into a bash terminal. That explains the customer behavior. :face_with_monocle:

docs-team: Thanks for flagging. Which exact docs page? I think it's /docs/api/rerank and the quickstart snippet for cURL. I can push a patch to standardize to `Content-Type: application/json` and `--data-raw`.

maria: Please include both a correct curl and an explicit note: "documents must be a JSON array of strings (not a JSON-encoded string)". Also show a bad example so customers know the pitfall.

docs-team: Agreed. Proposed doc snippet to replace the broken one:
```bash
# correct example
curl https://api.redwood.inference/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-raw '{"query":"best travel laptops","documents":["Dell XPS 13","MacBook Air"]}'

# bad example (DO NOT use)
# this serializes documents as a string and may produce validation errors or identical scores
curl ... --data-binary '{"query":"...","documents":"[\"A\",\"B\"]"}'
```

elaine: Support-bot created ticket INC-2026 for the customer and attached repro notes. @docs-team can you link the ticket once fixed?

support-bot: Ticket INC-2026 created and assigned to support. SLA: 48h. Logs and customer curl attached.

ken: Action items I propose:
- docs-team: update page + console snippet
- eng-runtime: add a stricter validation error that explicitly says "documents must be an array of strings" instead of generic 400 (will reduce confusion)
- support: reply with fixed curl and offer to validate customer's payload (done)

docs-team: I'll push a quick patch to docs and the console snippet generator — standardize on `--data-raw` and JSON content-type, and add the explicit note and broken-example. Will ping here when deployed.

maria: I replied to the customer with the corrected curl example and repro notes, offered to validate their new request. They tried it and confirmed scores look correct now. :) :thumbsup:

ryan: Can we add a small unit/integration test for the console snippet generator that pastes into bash and validates it parses as JSON (no embedded escaped-strings)? If not possible, at least add a linter rule for the generator templates.

docs-team: Noted. I'll add a template linter and a docs smoke test. ETA EOD tomorrow.

maria: Closing loop — customer is unblocked. Keeping thread open until docs PR and runtime validation ticket are merged. Thanks all.
